Kind of a funny story that happened the other day that I would like to share.

I have a friend who is a die hard Bernie fan. He says he is a democratic socialist and supports Bernie's policies. Talking to him about politics though something just didn't quite line up. Some of the things he was saying that he supported didn't quite line up with Bernie's socialist model like he doesn't support the government regulating industry(like Bernie is supporting.)

So I was thinking...maybe he doesn't really understand Democratic Socialism. So I sent him a link to a Nolan Chart(I'm sure we all have taken one from time to time, but if you haven't [Link](https://www.theadvocates.org/quiz/quiz.php) ) Anyway so he takes the test, and it comes back Right Moderate. My friend replies well isn't this where Sanders is at?

I send him this...[On the Issues Nolan Results for Bernie](http://www.ontheissues.org/Bernie_Sanders.htm)

Now he is really confused on who he supports. So I very nicely send him a link to the LP Website. I think we have a new member.
Democratic Socialism and the Nolan Chart.

Honestly, I don't the advocates quiz is that good. For one, it's really short. Second, the questions are almost all phrased in a way as to bias the inexperienced taker towards the libertarian postition. For example, "End 'corporate welfare.' No government handouts to business" is not a remotely neutral way to phrase it. Calling it "welfare" (which may be true, but I digress) is likely to bias a neutral reader to be against it. A more neutral way to phrase it might be something along the lines of "should the government ever provide financial support to private corporations?"

Think about how slightly changing the wording in a poll can produce dramatically different results. I think there's something similar going on with this advocates quiz.

I much prefer this quiz: http://www.quiz2d.com/

I feel that it isn't perfect, but an effort is made to phrase all the answers in a way advocates of such a position would actually phrase their support. I feel it's the best of these types of quizzes I have seen.

I left a part out of the story. Of course my friend doesn't blindly believe in something because a internet quiz said so...so I redirected him to the Nolan Chart on the On The Issues site. He got about the same results.

I give some leeway for kids.

Age 0-3: A baby/toddler has no control over their food except maybe be finicky. I hope everyone agrees that a fat baby/toddler is flat out child abuse and neglect.

Age 4-11: If you let your little kid get fat because you give into their demands to eat candy and sweet and mc donalds, that's bad parenting. They are CHILDREN. Age 12-17: This where puberty starts kicking in and unless you're an extra special level of abuse (home schooled, no internet, no access/highly controlled access to media) you should start getting an inkling that fat is at the very least unattractive to everyone and kills you dating prospects. 18-21... No excuses... if you parents are abusive, get out, find your own way...weight doesn't come off over night, but start the losing process and get human during these ages.
